VIETNAMESE BUDDHISM

PL:2545 - DL 2001

Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha

THE SAINT QUESTION - ANSWER

Ly Vien Tinh before the Chinese language

Mage An Quang appraises

Vietnamese translation: THICH GIAC NGUYEN

TRANSLATOR'S WORDS

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Questions and Answers and the Sacred Inspiration Book is a book belonging to the Mahayana Buddhist system, edited in Chinese by Layman Ly Vien Tinh and reviewed by Dharma Master An Quang. Buddhist Publishing Society published in Taipei, on July 30, 65th Republic year. (TL.1976).

The content includes Questions and Answers about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, as well as the story of his inspiration manifesting to save lives from ancient times and what has been heard recently. This material is found in the Tale of the God of Tang, the Tale of the High Monk, the Tale of the Layman, and the Characters of Cuu Hoa Mountain, all of which are fully recorded.

When it comes to Ksitigarbha Sutra and stories related to him, there are currently many controversies, claiming that it is not the Buddha's teachings. That's just a superstitious myth. Because most of it is scattered in the Tuc Tang, compiled and added by later generations.

Here we are not scholars so we don't have time to research carefully, but we can cite the words of Dharma Master Hoang Nhat in the appendix at the end of the book. Through his research and teaching work, the Dharma Master believes that in the Sutra Pitaka, only the book "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Ten Kings of Cause and Effect" is a pseudo-sutra that should not be popularized. I hope you read it and it will be clear.

As we know in Buddhism, famous great Bodhisattvas such as Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, Theravada... are the supreme Bodhisattvas who assist Śākyamuni Buddha in teaching and transforming living beings, often taking the form of lay followers, symbolizing the light of the same world. As for Ksitigarbha, he is the image of a monk who has escaped the world, holding a pearl in his hand, holding a staff in his hand, with widespread moral conduct and merit.

In particular, his great vow is always to thoroughly practice Bodhisattva conduct, to save the suffering of sentient beings in the six paths, especially the suffering in hell. If there were still a sentient being there who was tormented and suffering, he would still be a Bodhisattva and teach and not become a Buddha. Therefore, the manifestation of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is truly miraculous and inconceivable, with the purpose of awakening people to live with the truth, transforming the mind of ignorance, to achieve true happiness and joy.

There is nothing more beautiful than, in the middle of a world full of violence, hatred, unsatisfactoriness, and many distracting thoughts that arise like waves crashing on the shore, but to maintain a calm, calm mind like the earth. In quiet contemplation, contemplate the mysterious True Nature, revealing Wisdom. At that moment Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appeared, saving sentient beings from hell.

Currently, there are overseas Buddhists living in Los Angeles, California, USA, who are eager to learn and practice the vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. On their return visit to their homeland, Vietnam, in the summer of 1998, they came to Giac Nguyen Pagoda, District 4, Saigon, met me and gave me this booklet, asking them to translate it into Vietnamese.

Self-assessment as not having enough professional qualifications, but ventures to work with sincerity. Therefore, I asked Professor Nguyen Cong Danh, who teaches Chinese literature, to help review and edit the manuscript, but there are definitely still many shortcomings.

Again, we found that the Luc Premonition part is not suitable for the times and can easily be considered superstitious and mythical. But out of respect for the book and the requests of the faithful who asked for translation, it must be translated completely, and once published online, it will be omitted. We hope our readers will sympathize and respectfully ask our knowledgeable friends to please give us your feedback and correct any errors. Sincere thanks.

Am Foot Care, Saigon

Winter of the year Tan Ty 2001

THICH GIAC NGUYEN

Respect

Part One

Holy Virtue Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha

QUESTION – ANSWER

Q: What day is Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's holy birthday?

ANSWER : The 30th day of the 7th lunar month.

Q: Based on what?

ANSWER: During the Tang Dynasty, in the fourth year of Yonghui. To the East (China), there is the country of Silla (also known as Goryeo or Korea). Crown Prince Kim Kieu Giac (Kim Kyo-Gak), after becoming a monk, practicing the Great Vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, took a boat to China, went to Anhui province, climbed the Nine-Peak Mountain. Sitting upright for nearly seventy-five years, attained enlightenment on July 30, the 16th year of Tang Dynasty's reign. (Please see Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Attachments page 36)

Later, he entered samadhi again twenty years later. During the time of entering great samadhi, it is said that he manifested himself into the sufferings of Hell to save sentient beings from the dark realm. In the second year of King Duong Chanh Duc's reign, on the 30th day of the 7th lunar month, he became a saint (passed away) and started the stupa. Therefore Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha attained enlightenment and became a saint on the same day.

QUESTION: Is Cuu Hoa Mountain the Ashram of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER: That's right, Jiuhua Mountain Ashram in Qingyang County, Anhui Province. Every year in July, quite a large number of people come to make offerings and worship this mountain. Transportation is very convenient.

Q: Why is it that every time we recite the Holy Name, we often call the Great Vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER : The two words Great Vow are from the Ksitigarbha Original Vow Sutra that Buddha said. In her past life, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva was the daughter of a Brahmin lineage; used to be a child of a wealthy family; used to be a Saintess of Quang Muc; used to be King, etc.

“From now until countless eons later, because of the sins and sufferings of sentient beings in the six paths, I will establish many vast means to help all sentient beings be liberated, and then I myself will attain Buddhahood.”

When she became Saintess Quang Muc, she took another oath:

“In front of the image of the Tathagata with eyes as pure as a lotus flower (Pure Lotus Flower Mu), I vow that from now on forever, in hundreds of thousands of millions of eons, in any world where there are sentient beings falling into the three evil realms: hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, I vow to save all those sentient beings, keep them far away from the three evil paths, and all of them will become Buddhas, and then I will attain perfect enlightenment".

When he became king of a country, he made a great vow:

“If I do not first save those who suffer from sin, make them happy, and attain enlightenment and liberation, then I vow not to have become a Buddha.”

Therefore, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has experienced countless eons and saved countless sentient beings. Up to now, he is still a Bodhisattva and has not yet ascended the Buddha throne. The Bodhisattva's vow, simply put, is to save all sentient beings to attain Enlightenment. Hell is not yet empty, I vow not to become a Buddha. So, please see how great his vow is, nothing can compare to it.

Among the ranks of great Bodhisattvas, Manjushri represents Great Wisdom. Samantabhadra represents Great Virtue. Avalokiteśvara represents Great Compassion. As for Ksitigarbha, he represents the Great Vow of Śākyamuni Buddha himself in the Dharma assembly.

At the Dharma assembly, Śākyamuni Buddha declared:

“I vow to subdue sentient beings to be strong and strong, vow to escape the suffering of evil realms. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva preserves and supports my great vow, it is impossible to think and know it all.”

Question: I heard that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva only saves sentient beings in hell. Is that so?

ANSWER : In the Original Vows Sutra, Buddha said: "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has great karma for sentient beings in the Jambudvipa world. If we could tell about the beneficial things heard or seen in sentient beings, it would not be enough to say it in hundreds of thousands of eons." In the Contemplation Sutra, we see the Buddha speaking very clearly:

-"From the time Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva made the vow to make a vow until today, through countless, boundless, inconceivable kalpas of monks. Therefore, for a long time, this Bodhisattva has often saved sentient beings in the sea of suffering, full of merit, relying on his original vow of free divine power, manifesting in all ten directions. Although returning to a wide spectrum everywhere, often doing good merit in the middle of a world with five defilements. These are: life is fragile, seeing mistakes, afflictions and karma, sentient beings are strong and short-lived, but teaching to benefit all is deeply clear.

In the Dharma assembly, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has a dignified body, majestic and superior virtue, no one can compare except Tathagata. Furthermore, Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's transformation career covers the entire Sa-ba world, on par with Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, other great Bodhisattvas cannot compare. Because of the power of his vow, all sentient beings' wishes are quickly satisfied, the heavy sin karma of sentient beings can be transformed, all obstacles are eliminated, and they are immediately at peace."

The sutra says: "Bodhisattvas fear causes, living beings fear results." Saving results is of course inevitable, but preventing causes is even more urgent. Because the karmic karma of human beings continually creates Ten Unwholesome Deeds, after death they must suffer in hell. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has not yet saved all those who have suffered in hell, let alone those who are about to fall?

Q: I heard again that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's merit and benefits are superior to other great Bodhisattvas, is that true?

ANSWER: Most of the great Bodhisattvas are reincarnations of ancient Buddhas, who are not high or low. But because the Dharma conditions of sentient beings from many lifetimes up to now have been linked together, there is inevitably some depth and some shallowness; Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in this world has great karma. The reason why the World-Honored One praised Ksitigarbha above all was to make sentient beings have strong faith and gain many benefits. Therefore, in the Ten Wheel Sutra, Buddha said:

If there is a person who sincerely takes refuge in the name, chants, worships, and makes offerings to the Great Bodhisattvas in hundreds of lifetimes, hoping to have their wishes fulfilled. It's not as good as someone who, within one meal, wholeheartedly takes refuge, confesses his name, chants, worships and makes offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, and all his prayers will quickly be fully accomplished. (Central Summary) Thus, the Great Being, in order to mature the sentient beings, has long strived to practice with great vows and immense compassion, and is more courageous and diligent than other Bodhisattvas. Therefore, you should make offerings."

In the Prime Prayer it also says:

“Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has great karma in the Jambudvipa world. Like the great Bodhisattvas Manjushri, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteshvara, and Maitreya, they also manifest hundreds of thousands of salvation bodies in the six paths, but sometimes their vows are not yet fulfilled. Meanwhile, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva vows to teach all sentient beings in the six paths, throughout countless eons as many as the number of sands in hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges rivers, it is truly limitless. end.

Question: When we worship and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, how do we ultimately gain merit and benefits?

ANSWER : The merits and benefits of worshiping and making offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva cannot be exhausted.

Q: Which benefits are most obvious?

ANSWER: Anyone who wants to pray for blessings and wisdom from the Bodhisattva cannot help but pray in this present life. For example, when going abroad, traveling, having a new son or daughter, and having a serious or serious illness, all are effectively inspired.

Q: While traveling, what are the benefits of worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

Question: What are the benefits of worshiping Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha when a son or daughter is born?

QUESTION: What are the benefits of worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER: The sutra says: "If any sentient being, when their life is about to end, hears a sentence of Bodhisattva's name passing through their ears, then after death they will be far away from the suffering of the three evil paths. At that time, like their parents, relatives and relatives, for the sick person, they will paint or draw the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva for the sick person. Or make the person seriously ill before their death. Seeing and hearing about this action, their karma will be eliminated and they will be able to live longer. But if that person's life has ended, and because of their sin karma, they will fall into hell, their karma will be eliminated and they will be born in the heaven and human world, enjoying wonderful joy."

Question: What are the benefits of worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER: The sutra says: "If there is a living being who is sick and paralyzed forever in bed, unable to wish to live, unable to wish to die. At night, he often dreams of ghosts appearing, or sees deceased relatives, or strays into danger, or walks with ghosts and spirits, over time his illness gets worse and worse, and in his sleep he cries out in pain. This is all because karma has not been determined in terms of severity or lightness, so either difficult to die, or difficult to heal.

Therefore, you must face the statues of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and recite this sutra loudly once. Or take the patient's personal favorite things, such as clothes, precious jewelry, fields, gardens, houses, etc., stand in front of the patient and loudly say: "We Full name ....... now for this patient, in front of the Sutra, bring all the money and wealth, use it to give alms and offerings, print and send out Sutras, or embellish Buddha and Bodhisattva images, or build pagodas and stupas, or light oil lamps, or make offerings to permanent residences (Three said)”.

Sing this three times so that the patient can hear clearly. Like a sick person whose breathing has stopped, from one day to seven days, keep reciting this sutra loudly. After that person dies, even if he committed a serious crime in his previous life, he will be freed from it.

Question: There are ten days of fasting each month, what are the benefits of worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva on these days?

ANSWER : A lot. The sutra says: "For sentient beings in the realm of Southern Jambudvipa, that is, this world, every single movement or thought is nothing but karma, (not to mention those who indulge in evil deeds).

Each month, the ten days of fasting are the 1st, 8th, 14th, 15th, 18th, 23rd, 24th, 28th, 29th and 30th. You should stand in front of Buddha and Bodhisattva statues and recite the Ksitigarbha Original Vow once, then for about a hundred yojanas around your residence, you will be far away from disasters. As for the people in that family, regardless of age, young or old, now or in the future, they will not encounter any hardships, will not suffer from unexpected illnesses, and will have plenty of food and clothing.

Question: According to legend, Ksitigarbha practiced to the realm of great vows and attained Tathagatagarbha nature; The Ten Wheel Sutra says that when Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva is about to come to a Dharma meeting, everyone will gain more understanding and strength, like an athlete whose body is heavy and difficult to lift. So does it benefit people to stay at home and work in the fields, worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER:Yes, the Jataka Sutra says:

“In the land where you live, find a clean place to the south, use soil, stone, bamboo and wood to make an altar. In it, paint an image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or use gold, silver, soil, stone, wood, create statues, burn incense to make offerings, worship, and praise, then the place that person lives will receive ten benefits:

1. Fertile sandy soil.

2. The house is forever safe .

3. Those who fall are born in Heaven.

4. People still benefit.

5. Wishing you satisfaction.

6. From water and fire.

7. Eliminate damage.

8. Completely put an end to nightmares.

9. In and out of the divine protection.

10. Often meet Saints.

Q: Please tell us more about the benefits of people working in the fields worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

ANSWER: The Ten Rings Sutra says: "According to the place of residence, if sentient beings take seeds and plant them in wild fields, or well-plowed fields. Whether they diligently take care of them, or do not take care of them at the right time, as if they single-mindedly recite the name, chant, pay homage to, and make offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, then that good man will gain wonderful merit and majestic concentration, causing all their trees and fruits to grow. have a good harvest. Why is this? Because this Good Man has gone through countless kalpas, in countless Buddhas and World-Honored Ones, making great and steadfast vows.

Due to this aspiration, in order to mature all sentient beings like that, it often protects and cares for all the great earth, often protects and cares for all seeds, and often makes sentient beings use it at will. Such was the divine power of that good man that he often caused all the plants, roots, shoots, branches, leaves, and fruits to grow all over the earth. Have a good season. The medicinal plants, rice and beans, sprouts, and fruits are all so lush, soft and beautiful, with a pure fragrance.

QUESTION: Please elaborate more on the benefits of worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

ANSWER: The Original Vow Sutra says: If there are sentient beings who see the image of Ksitigarbha and hear this Original Vow Sutra, then recite it. Using scents, flowers, food, drinks, clothes, and precious possessions to give alms, make offerings, praise, and worship, will receive 28 benefits:

1. Heaven and dragon protect.

2. The good fruit grows bigger.

3. Cultivate the Holy virtues.

4. The Enlightened Mind does not retreat.

5. Dress fully.

6. No illness .

7. From water and fire .

8. Don't get robbed.

9. People feel admiration .

10. The devil protects .

11. After transforming into a boy

12. Becoming a noble child.

13. Beautiful body.

14. Always born in heaven .

15. Annoying kings .

16. Bright mind, intelligent network .

17. Wishing for your satisfaction .

18. Beloved and happy .

19. Extermination disasters .

20. Completely eliminate karma .

21. Travel well .

22. Peaceful dream night .

23. Immortals avoid falling.

24. Born to enjoy blessings.

25. The Saints praise .

26. Benefits and clarity .

27. Rich in Compassion .

28. Ultimately becoming a Buddha .

QUESTION: Will the benefits be greater when generating enlightenment and making offerings to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER: Yes, the Sutra says: If there are good men and women who want to develop great compassion to save all sentient beings, want to attain Supreme Bodhi, and want to leave the three realms. Those people see images and hear the name Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha; If you wholeheartedly take refuge, make offerings, and worship, your prayers will quickly be achieved."

Question: Besides the benefits of worshiping Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, is there anything else that can be done?

ANSWER : There are many more. As you can read the Ksitigarbha Original Vow Sutra from the sixth, eleventh to thirteenth chapters.

Question: Does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva have any premonitions?

ANSWER : It says a lot in the Proverbs. During the Song Dynasty, people often carefully recorded the miracles of the phenomenon of Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha. We can collect some special ones in the book The Inspiration of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Origins. Of course, it is not possible to write everything completely.

Question: Is there a difference between the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER ; No difference, everyone can chant the same. Many of the sutras mention the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Only the Mahayana Sutra of the Bodhisattva Mind and Heart of Bodhisattva mentions the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Q: What types of sutras talk about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva?

ANSWER: There are the Ksitigarbha Original Vows Sutra, the Ten Wheels Sutra, the Contemplation Sutra, and even in the Diamond Samadhi Sutra and the Great Samadhi Sutra, all of which have teachings mentioned. There are not a few sutras mentioning the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Normally, most people chant the Ksitigarbha Vow Sutra. Master Linh Thang composed a commentary, and recently Mr. Ho Trach Pham wrote a Bach Dialogue that explains quite well. The Contemplation Sutra is proclaimed by Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha and composed by Great Master Ngan Ich.

Q: How many types of writings and translations related to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can be recited?

ANSWER : Great Master Ngan Ich created the book Praise Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Repentance and Vows and Contemplation of Dharma Practices, of course very good. Until recently, Dharma Master Hoang Nhat compiled the book Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Great Bodhisattva. Lu The Marquis painted a painting praising the story of Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha at Cuu Hoa Mountain. Dharma Master An Quang reviewed and edited the writings at Cuu Hoa Son, Mr. Uong Phung Tri's diary talks about a past life where Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha saved his mother, and in Mr. Hoa Quat's book, the book about Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's Inspiration, etc....all can be read and referenced.

Question: You are a lay practitioner, often chanting the Ksitigarbha Vow Sutra. Please clearly state your feelings about this sutra.

ANSWER : We read the Original Prayer Sutra up to the chapter on the Karma and Karma of sentient beings. First, we must know that the karmic fate of living beings is important. Reading the chapter Chuc Luy Nhon Thien (instructions to save Gods and humans), one must know that the compassion of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is very deep and wide. Reading the chapter Divine Powers in the Heavenly Palace, you must know that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva makes a very great vow. We are living in a life where many great disasters occur. You should only sincerely return to revere the Great Vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Q: Does Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva teach us any practical methods to practice?

ANSWER : Yes, he taught us to always recite Buddha's name. Living in the age of the end of dharma, it is necessary to take the Buddhist recitation method as the most stable method. In the chapter Proclaiming the Buddha's Name of the Original Prayer Sutra, of course the names of the Buddhas are clearly listed. Furthermore, it is clearly stated in the Ten Wheel Sutra:

“When I leave this body, I pray to be born in the Buddha realm.

Meet Amitabha. Almost close to the Buddhas.

Received Buddha empowerment. It's okay.

Return to the mortal world. The level of love is everywhere,

Agree on the true nature.”

Question: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has made such a vast vow, why is the karma of sentient beings still deep?

ANSWER : Look clearly at the Prime Prayer Sutra from the third to the fifth chapter. In it, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva once mentioned the principles of cause and effect and retribution, and the sentient beings who experience retribution in hell, all explained very clearly and delicately.

For all sinners, Bodhisattvas speak to them about each type of crime. If you don't repent, you will have to fall into hell to suffer. Among the many types of hell, the Unending Hell is the most painful. Because suffering never stops, it is called Infinite; Whether it is one person or many people, the body can fill the entire prison, so it is called Vo Cock; The punishments are constantly suffering, so it is called Infinite.

Q: What types of sins deserve to fall into the Unending Hell?

ANSWER: One is to be unfilial or kill one's parents.

Third is harming the Three Jewels' permanent pillars, offending monks and nuns. Or in the temple, let loose and commit adultery. Or kill or harm living creatures.

Fourth, being a monk but not having a mind like that of a monk, abusing and wasting what is permanent. (For example, taking money from the Three Jewels to buy things for yourself and your family. Bribing people to seek fame and fortune, gambling and drinking, spending wastefully), deceiving lay people, violating the precepts, and committing many crimes.

The fifth is stealing from the temple such as money, utensils, rice, food, clothes, etc. to the point of taking something without giving it. Those people must fall into the Hell of No Interruption, never hoping to get out.

QUESTION: How to know the profound compassion of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas?

ANSWER: Buddha Shakyamuni in the Dao Loi heaven, stretched out his golden arm and rubbed the buds of hundreds of thousands of billions of millions of incarnations of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and said: "I have spent countless lifetimes laboring and liberating such strong-willed sentient beings who are full of sin and suffering and are difficult to enlighten. In addition, there are those who have not been tamed and must receive retribution according to their karma. If they fall into an evil path and suffer many sufferings, then You should think of me in the Dao Loi heaven, having graciously entrusted you with the effort to save all sentient beings in this Sa-ba world until Maitreya is born, they are all completely liberated, far from all suffering, and meet the Buddha."

In the chapter Wishing Luy Nhon Thien, the Buddha rubbed Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's head again, praising Bodhisattva's inconceivable divine power; Compassion is inconceivable; The talent is inconceivable. And he also sincerely and thoughtfully brought all the gods and humans and sentient beings, those who were in the house of fire, and had not yet left the three realms, to entrust to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. If there are people in heaven who plant a few good roots in the Buddhadharma, Bodhisattvas will protect and teach them, making the good roots grow and not letting them lose the Bodhi mind. If there is a person who falls into an evil path and only knows how to recite a Buddha's name, a Bodhisattva's name, or recite a sentence, a verse, or a Mahayana sutra, the Bodhisattva should use divine means to save them from sin and suffering, manifest their boundless body to destroy hell, and cause them to be born in heaven to enjoy happiness. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva said with every word: "May the World-Honored One not be worried." Therefore we can see that the compassion of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas is very deep.

QUESTION: What is the meaning of testament?

ANSWER : The meaning of the will is extremely important. Because all sentient beings suffering from sin and suffering in the present and future lives are entrusted by the World-Honored One, all are gathered into the power of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Compassionate Vow. Thanks to that, all sentient beings know where to take refuge. Those sentient beings that Buddha has not yet saved will be saved by Ksitigarbha. Because the Buddha's vow is also the Bodhisattva's vow. Bodhisattva's loving kindness is also the loving kindness of the World-Honored One, so Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva helped him. In other words, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can be considered as Buddha.

Q: Is there any other meaning?

Question: I am so grateful and so happy! Thanks to that, I knew where to return to farm. I vow to pay homage to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva every day. Please can you compose a dedication prayer for me?

ANSWER : Okay, that's good. I have compiled a verse: Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Dedication Vow Ceremony, everyone can apply it as follows:

FOREWORD

The story of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's inspiration.

Mage An Quang.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, the vow is wide and deep. Although he fully realized the nature of the Dharma a long time ago, he did not abide in the realm of Eternal Light and did not attain Buddhahood. He has great compassion, widespread throughout all realms. Depending on the moment, he appears to save sentient beings, and is often in darkness to save all sentient beings suffering extreme suffering in hell.

According to ancient legend, Bodhisattva once made a Great Vow; Only when all sentient beings are saved will they attain Bodhi. If hell is not empty, you will not become a Buddha. Because the minds of sentient beings and Buddha are inseparable.

Due to confusion, in the eternal truth, delusions give birth to madness, greed, anger and ignorance arise, creating karma of killing, stealing, and adultery, leading to the six-fold cycle of reincarnation, with no day of escape. Few people are born in the heavenly world, many fall into the three evil paths.

For example, if a precious pearl falls into a toilet, a foolish person will see it as filth and will not love or regret it. Wise people know that it is a priceless jewel. tieu_de: The holy relics of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva
noi_dung:
I- Bodhisattva Earth Store

1) SACRED RELICS OF Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha

Buddha Shakyamuni once told Bodhisattva Universally Extensive: "You must know that Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva has hundreds of thousands of billions of millions of great divine power, bringing so many benefits to sentient beings, it is impossible to say it all. The sentient beings in this Jambudvipa world have a very good relationship with Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Whoever hears the name of Bodhisattva, or sees the image of Bodhisattva, has heard this sutra for about three or five words. a sentence, a verse, then those people will be incredibly happy now. And in hundreds of thousands of future lives, they will be born into a noble family with a dignified body."

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's career in saving sentient beings is no less than Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara's. At Dao Loi heaven, Śākyamuni Buddha praised and praised Ksitigarbha's merits and taught Avalokiteśvara to spread widely. Therefore, we can see that the two Great Bodhisattvas both have a deep connection with sentient beings in this world. People in the world know a lot about Avalokiteśvara saving sentient beings, but very little is seen or heard about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's teachings, and then Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva only saves sinful and suffering sentient beings in hell, and has nothing to do with sentient beings in the human world. This is so wrong.

If we read the entire book, we will clearly understand that sentient beings want to pray for the Bodhisattva's Blessings and blessings. Not only in this life, there is nothing they cannot pray for, but they also have to wait until after death. Moreover, the sutras say: "Bodhisattvas fear the cause, living beings fear the effect." Saving consequences is of course inevitable, but saving causes is more urgent.

Beings in the human world who commit ten evil karma will surely suffer in hell in the future. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva thought about the suffering and suffering in hell, in order to save the suffering of sins, what about the karma that has not yet fallen?

That Great Bodhisattva, regarding the differences in each place, displays teachings depending on the conditions, we do not have the Dharma Eye (Dharma Eye), that is, we cannot know. But we in China have thousands of authentic stories about the cumulative transformation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, all concentrated here in Jiuhua Mountain, Anhui Province.

Our country has four famous mountains of four great ashrams. Like Nam Hai, Putuo Mountain is the ashram of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. In Son Tay, Ngu Dai Mountain is the ashram of Bodhisattva Manjushri. In Sichuan, Emei Mountain is the ashram of Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. In Anhui, Cuu Hoa Mountain is the ashram of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

Every year in July, countless people go to Cuu Hoa Mountain to travel to the homeland. Because July 30 is the day Bodhisattva attained enlightenment. Because I had the opportunity to come here once, I should present the story of Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's incarnation as well as the establishment of Ksitigarbha's ashram at Cuu Hoa mountain. Please watch and remember forever:

1,240 years after Buddha passed away. To the Northeast of our country (China), there is Silla (Silla) also known as Korea (Korea). Crown Prince Kim Kieu Giac (Kim Kyo-Gak), the son of the king of that country, was born in the 7th century, in 696 BC, now Hanoi, in South Korea.

Even though he lives in luxurious luxury, golden palaces, and jade palaces, the prince's personality is frugal and is not affected by the royal lifestyle of luxury and enjoyment. He only cares about learning and loves to read books of saints and sages. With his dignified appearance and pure compassion, it is difficult for anyone to match him.

In the fourth year of Vinh Huy, Emperor Cao Tong's reign. After consulting all the Three Teachings, the Nine Streams and the Hundred Schools of Chu Tu, he exclaimed: "Compared with the Six Classics of Confucianism and the Taoism of the Immortals, the First Noble Truth of Buddhism is the most superior, very compatible with my aspirations." After that, the prince practiced the Bodhisattva practice in the hope of relieving suffering from the three paths and established the intention to become a monk at the age of 24.

On a bright moonlit night, the Crown Prince carried a white mastiff dog and silently sailed away from Nhan Xuyen wharf (Incheon), across the sea to the West, to Thanh Duong district, Trizhou prefecture, Anhui province, China. After many days of wandering, he found his way to the Cuu Hoa mountain complex, saw the charming, solemn and beautiful landscape, and sat in meditation on the top of Cuu Tu for seventy-five years. Mountain gods and monkeys often make offerings of fruits and flowers.

In the sixteenth year of Tang Xuanzong's reign. On the night of July 30, he realized his true mind and achieved enlightenment. At that time, at the foot of Cuu Hoa mountain, there was a rich man who owned the whole mountain area. People called him Cong Man (Old man surnamed Man), he was also known as Van Cac old man. For many years he has been diligent in doing good deeds, often vowing to offer vegetarian meals to one hundred monks around the area, but each time there are only ninety-nine monks, and the only monk, Kim Kieu Giac, or Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, has not been invited because he is in seclusion and deep meditation on a high mountain.

He came down from the mountain and went to Notary Man Man's house. Then he asked the homeowner for a piece of land the size of a Y sheet (Ca sa). Man Cong said: "-All of Cuu Hoa Mountain is my land. Please choose as you like." At that time, the Bodhisattva grabbed his robe and spread it over the nine mountain tops. Man Cong was very happy to see that. So Cuu Hoa Mountain was dedicated to the Bodhisattva.

Min Cong also had a son who, because of his admiration for his morality, asked to become a monk and was given the Dharma name Dao Minh. (After twenty-five years) Man Cong also left the habit of becoming a monk and practicing Buddhism. Because becoming a monk comes first and then follows the Ha La (age of religion), so he had to bow to his son and honor him as his master. Therefore, later, the statue of Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha was accompanied on the left by a young monk, Dao Minh, and on the right, by an Elder, Man Cong. And the Daoist mastiff's name is Thien Thinh.

The Bodhisattva later entered samadhi for twenty years. It is said that during this time he descended to the dark places to preach the Dharma of salvation to those who were condemned to the sufferings of hell.

In the first year of Chi Duc (TL 765), there was the famous scholar Gia Cat Tiet, living in a village at the foot of the mountain, guiding the elders in the village to go up the mountain to enjoy. When arriving at the flat land on the mountain, we saw clouds drifting lazily in the blue sky with warm sunshine, the sound of a stream gurgling from the ravine, the sound of birds chirping in the shady forest trees, making everyone fascinated by the beautiful scenery. As we gradually entered the deep forest, we suddenly saw a Zen Master meditating on a rock next to the stream, eyes closed in a state of meditation. Next to it is an old three-legged urn with one leg missing, in which there is still a little rice mixed with white clay. A moment later, the Zen master came out of meditation, took rice mixed with soil, cooked it, and ate it. After eating, he continued to meditate quietly. When the people in the group saw that, they were extremely moved and came to tell him: "Dear master! You practice asceticism like this, this is the fault of our villagers!" Soon, everyone in the village worked together to build a large Zen temple, offering food all year round without interruption.

In the first year of Kien Trung (TL. 780), the Prefect Truong Nghiem, out of respect for his noble conduct, reported to Emperor Duc Tong, issuing an official edict to build the Monastery. At that time, Ksitigarbha's Ashram was truly majestic and solemn.

At that time, the monks of Silla (Silla) heard about his reputation, and a few hundred people came to study with him. Gradually, the number of people increased and food became scarce. One day, he went outside the temple and dug up a lot of powdery white clay to supplement his diet as he used to do. Everyone in the temple, impressed by his virtue, spoke together: "We vow to use the dharma of joy and food and meditation to nourish our wisdom and life, and not use food to support this impermanent body and life."

One ​​day, on the first day of Autumn in the tenth year of Trinh Nguyen (TL. 795), He summoned the Sangha into the Main Hall to instruct the audience. People feel confused for no reason. At that time, the mountains emitted the pitiful screams of animals. Large rocks thundered down into the abyss, thousands of trees and plants withered everywhere, and clouds covered them. Heaven and earth shook, and the fragrant scent spread throughout the area. He sat cross-legged and passed away on July 30, the second year of Chanh Duc, 795 AD. Abiding in the 99th Spring and Autumn.

There are documents that say that after his death, his physical body was enshrined in a stone cave, but three years later, the Sangha opened the stone cave and found that his physical body remained intact like a statue. The crowd took their bodies to the stupa on Than Quang Lanh mountain. Along the road, it sounded like the sound of a staff rattling along with everyone's footsteps.

Thus, his life and career of practice and enlightenment are similar to the vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, which in the Original Vows Sutra, the Buddha preached at the Dao Loi heaven. Therefore, at that time the Chinese honored him as the Holy Monk, the reincarnation of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Since then, Jiuhua Mountain, Anhui province has become the great ashram of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. (This part is translated according to the book and extracted from Korean Buddhist historical documents.)

If we were to recount the deeds of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva saving sentient beings, as the Buddha proclaimed, it would not be possible to tell them all in hundreds of thousands of eons. Up to the above mentioned miracles are true in the Eastern Land, but in the Tale of the God of Tang, the Tale of the Cao Tang, the Tale of the Layman, and the Characters of Cuu Hoa Mountain, they are all fully recorded.

tieu_de: The past causes and conditions of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva
noi_dung:
2)- PAST CAUSES OF Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha

Why did Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's great vow to save sentient beings arise? Just knowing the causes and conditions of a Bodhisattva's past life can be clear enough.

The Bodhisattva in her past life was a child of a rich man, a Brahmin's daughter, a King, and a Holy Maiden of Light, all of which are clearly recorded in the Sutra of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows. Now just briefly talk about the two events that he was the son of a wealthy man and the daughter of a Brahmin.

First of all, let's talk about a time long ago, a long time ago, when the Buddha with the title Lion, Tan Tan, Perfection of Ten Thousand Hanh Tathagata, was born, at that time Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha was still an ordinary person, the son of a wealthy family. He saw the Buddha's perfect appearance and dignity, and his heart was filled with joy. Therefore, he bowed his head and asked Tathagata how he had that good body?

The rich man's son immediately stood before the Buddha and made a vow: "From now on, I vow that from now on, for all sentient beings suffering from sin and suffering in the six paths, I will establish methods of salvation. After all of them become Buddhas, only then will I myself become a Buddha. If the world still has six paths of reincarnation and three paths of evil, I also vow to become a Bodhisattva and save sentient beings."

The reason Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha has made that great vow since he was before the Tathagata, the Lion of Joyful Attachment, and up to now, has gone through countless countless great kalpas that cannot be fully described, helping limitless sentient beings that cannot be counted. Until now he is still a Bodhisattva without becoming a Buddha.

Let's talk about a long time ago when the Buddha named Giac Hoa Dinh Tu Tai King was born. At that time, there was a Brahman saint who believed in Buddhism very much, but her mother did not believe in it and even slandered the Three Jewels.

Therefore, the Saint knew that while her mother was still alive, due to her mistakes, after death she would have to endure all kinds of suffering in hell. The saint then sold all the things in the house and did major Dharma work such as renovating the temple tower to worship King Tathagata.

One day, with a sincere heart and feeling the Buddha's inspiration, the Saint while walking suddenly heard a voice in the void saying: You really want to know where your mother was born, right? So quickly return and remember Buddha, you will understand clearly. The saint immediately returned home, sat upright, and single-mindedly recited the name of the Enlightened Flower Samadhi King Tathagata for an entire day and night. Suddenly I found myself reaching a beach, the water in that sea was boiling, there were many people diving. I saw demons and wild beasts, beating and devouring them, suffering all kinds of suffering, looking so pitiful that I didn't dare look at them for long.

At that time, suddenly a Demon King came and bowed to welcome him. The saint then asked: "Venerable sir, what place is this?" The Demon King replied: "This is the shore of Hell. People in the world who kill, steal, commit adultery, lie, argue, curse, and carry many sins of karma, die in forty-nine days without a relative to help them repent and do good, so they must fall into this sea. To the east of this sea there is another sea of suffering. Then to the east of that sea there is another sea, the suffering in which is even greater. Through three more Such a deep sea of karma is the realm of hell, with more and more unspeakable suffering."

The holy woman then asked the Demon King: "Please tell me where my mother is currently reborn?" At the same time, tell the mother's name, date of birth and death. The Demon King examined and said: "She originally went to Hell to suffer, but because she had a filial daughter who did good deeds on her behalf, she was just reborn in heaven three days ago."

At that time, the Saint suddenly woke up as if from a dream. Knowing that his mother had passed away, he stood in front of the tower statue worshiping the Bodhisattva Buddha, Enlightenment, Concentration of Self-Consistency, King Tathagata, and made a great vow:

“From now on, I vow to endure all sentient beings suffering in the three evil paths from now on until the future. If hell is not empty, I vow not to become a Buddha.” Therefore Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha is still a Bodhisattva to this day.

We already know the past causes and conditions of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in general and clearly. Bodhisattvas once made a very broad vow in their past lives to save suffering and bring joy to all sentient beings. If all sentient beings receive the vow of suffering, then they will become Buddhas.

The reason Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha's incarnations fill all the worlds of the ten directions, each world manifests hundreds of thousands of billions of billions of bodies, each body transforms into hundreds of millions of millions of people, causing them to take refuge in the Three Jewels, far away from the suffering of birth and death, to reach Nirvana of ultimate happiness. Therefore, while reciting the Bodhisattva's holy name, we often call Namo Great Vow Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

“If there are people in the heavens who have planted a little good root in the Buddha Dharma, then you should also support their teachings and make them grow bigger and not let them slip away. If they fall into the evil realm, just recite the name of a Buddha, a Bodhisattva, the same sentence, a verse, a Mahayana sutra. You should also use your divine power to save them, manifest your boundless body to destroy hell, and let them be born in heaven to enjoy peace. happy”.

It can be seen that the Tathagata protects and recites sentient beings like parents who love their children, know clearly the illnesses and sufferings of their children, and think of hundreds of thousands of medical means to treat them. Although he endured all kinds of bitterness, he did not harbor resentment. When he was about to die and worried that they had lost their parents, he solemnly and thoughtfully entrusted his love for his foolish children to kind friends and relatives, so that they could help them, and when he died, he would have no regrets.

We today create many sins and deserve to suffer miserable consequences. Because of me, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva protects every thought and helps every hour. It is difficult because our eyes of the path have not yet been revealed, we have not seen the appearance of the Great Master, we have not listened to the teachings of the Great Master who once saved us from the world of birth and death, and we are beholden to him without understanding. Just like the sun shines everywhere but blind people have never received that benefit, so they don't see it or know it. How pitiful!

Alas! Śākyamuni Buddha's endless compassion, Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva accepted the Buddha's blessing, and his compassion is also endless. I only hope that everyone can quickly end evil, do good, and respect the Three Jewels. They will surely be protected by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

tieu_de: The beneficial merits of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva
noi_dung:
3) MERITS AND BENEFITS OF Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva of course has great karma with sentient beings in this world. So what merits and benefits do we gain by making offerings to Bodhisattvas? In the Ksitigarbha Original Vows Sutra, chapter Karma of Sentient Beings in the Jambudvipa Realm, chapter Tathagata's Praise, chapter Earth God Protects the Dharma, chapter Seeing and Hearing Are Beneficial, chapter Blessings of Gods and Men. In all of those chapters there is a very clear autobiography. Now just briefly:

“Then Śākyamuni Buddha said to Universal Bodhisattva: -If any living being hears the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, or clasps his hands, or praises, or prostrates, or is attached to him, then that person will be freed from thirty lifetimes of sin and suffering.

If any living being draws an image of a Bodhisattva, or molds an image of gold, silver, bronze, or stone, once he admires it, once he bows, then that person will be reborn in the thirty-third heaven a hundred times, far away from evil paths.

If there are sentient beings in front of the Bodhisattva statue who sing music, sing songs, praise, use scents and flowers to make offerings to encourage one person or many people, then in this life and in the next life there will always be good gods to protect them, far away from all evil.

If there is any sentient being who is paralyzed in bed forever in pain, unable to wish to live, unable to wish to die. Or at night you dream of demons appearing in the form of relatives in your house, or walking down a dangerous path, or walking with demons. Because of that, the illness became more and more severe, and in his sleep he cried out in pain, misery, and unhappiness. These are all treated by karma and have not been clearly defined as light or heavy, so it is either difficult to heal or difficult to die.

At that time, ordinary eyes of course cannot make people understand anything, one should only face the statues of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and loudly recite the Sutra of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows once. Or take the patient's favorite personal items, clothes, valuables, etc. stood in front of the sick person and said loudly: "We of that name, now for the sick person in front of the sutra statue, please bring these objects to sell, to make offerings to the sutra statue, or to create Buddha and Bodhisattva images, or to build pagodas and stupas, or to buy oil lamps to light offerings, or to make offerings to the Three Jewels' permanent pillars."

Sing it three times so that the patient can hear it clearly. If a sick person has stopped breathing, from one day to seven days he should still speak loudly as above and recite this Sutra loudly. After that person dies, no matter what sins they committed before, they will be freed from them.

If there are any sentient beings or see someone reciting the Sutra of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows. Even if one thought of praising or respecting this sutra occurs, you must use hundreds of thousands of means to advise that person to be diligent and not to retreat, and they will gain inconceivable merit.

If any living being dreams of seeing images of ghosts and spirits. Then you feel sad, cry, or feel sad and afraid, it's all because the relatives in the past have fallen into evil and have not been able to get out, and don't know what blessings to expect to save them. As before, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas keep their hearts steadfast in reading and reciting this sutra, or invite others to read and recite it three or seven times. Thanks to that merit, all are liberated. Until when I sleep, I no longer have nightmares.

If there is a lowly person who lives without freedom, needs to repent of his previous life's sins and recite the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva ten thousand times, then in hundreds of thousands of lives in the future he will often be born into a noble family.

If any woman has just given birth to a son or daughter within seven days, she should also recite this prayer. Recite the Bodhisattva's name ten thousand times, and the newly born child, if any trouble it has caused in its previous life, will be completely eliminated, will be happy and grow up quickly, and its blessed life will increase.

For sentient beings in the Jambudvipa world, all actions and thoughts are nothing but sinful karma. So usually on the ten days of each month, including the 1st, 8th, 14th, 15th, 18th, 23rd, 24th, 28th, 29th and 30th (the days when bad karma is grouped together), one should read and recite this entire Sutra in front of statues of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, while surrounding the place of residence, away from disasters. Everyone in that house for hundreds of thousands of years, far away from evil, had plenty of food and clothing, blessings came, disasters went away.

At that time, the Earth God Kien Lao knelt before Śākyamuni Buddha like this:

-“At one's residence in the South, choose a clean place, use soil, stone, bamboo, wood, build a page, a room, in which the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva can be drawn or use metal, stone, wood to cast a statue, burn incense to make offerings, worship and praise, then the place that person lives will receive ten benefits:

1- Fertile sandy soil.

2- Eternal home.

3- The dead give birth to Heaven.

4- People still benefit.

5- Wishing for satisfaction.

6- No fire or water accident.

7- Eliminate damage.

8- End nightmares completely.

9- Enter and exit the Divine Protection.

10- Often meet Saints.”

Buddha Shakyamuni told Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara:

-“If there are sentient beings who, while dying, hear the Bodhisattva's name with a piercing sound in their ears, after death they will be far away from the three paths of suffering. Or at that time, relatives took the patient's possessions and painted Bodhisattva images, causing the patient who was about to lose his sight and hearing to do these things. Okay, so much of that person's karma, if he gets seriously ill, he will be cured and live longer.

If there are any sentient beings who are young and have lost their parents, siblings, and when they grow up, they will remember those who have passed away. If you want to know where they will be reborn, that person can, for example, from one day to seven days, or paint an image of a Bodhisattva, hear his name, see his image, pay his respects, and make offerings without losing his original good heart. Even if that person's relatives and relatives fall into evil paths, they will still be liberated and reborn in the human world or the heavenly world to enjoy wonderful joy. As for those who have been born in the heavenly world or the human world, they will be transferred to the level of Sainthood and enjoy immeasurable peace and joy.

If within twenty-one days, one wholeheartedly worships the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and recites his name ten thousand times, the Bodhisattva will appear and show him where his relatives will be born. Or in the dream you will see and know your relatives. If you can chant the Bodhisattva's name a thousand times a day for up to a thousand days, the Bodhisattva will make the earth gods, ghosts and spirits stay in your place, follow the guardian for the rest of your life, enjoy all happiness in this life and have the Bodhisattva rub your head and receive prophecies.

If there are any sentient beings who want to develop compassion and save sentient beings. If they want to escape the three realms and practice the path of Supreme Enlightenment, those people often see the image and hear the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, wholeheartedly rely on it, make offerings, worship, and praise, then their prayers will definitely be fulfilled, and all their wishes will be satisfied.

If there are any sentient beings who read and recite Mahayana sutras without clearly understanding them, but when they hear the name and see the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, they buy enough beautiful scents, flowers, and offerings to respectfully present it. Use a bowl of clear water to place in front of the Bodhisattva image for one day and one night, then respectfully clasp your hands together to drink, facing the South. When water enters the mouth, one must be solemn and serious. After drinking, one must eat five pungent things: onions, chives, compresses, garlic, and palanquin; Abstaining from alcohol, meat, adultery, lying and killing, for seven days or twenty-one days, that person will see in a dream the image of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva appearing in his boundless body, pouring water on his head. After waking up, he immediately became intelligent. Once he heard the Mahayana sutras, he remembered them forever.

If there is a living being who is not well-fed, has many illnesses, or has an insecure home, he is often frightened in his dreams. Encountering many misfortunes and sufferings, if they respectfully recite Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's name ten thousand times, they will naturally overcome the misfortunes and be blessed with happiness.

If there are any sentient beings who have to enter the mountains, forests, rivers, or seas due to some fate, before going, they should recite the name of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva ten thousand times. If they do so, then wherever they go, they will have the earth ghosts and spirits to protect them from harm."

Buddha Shakyamuni declared to Bodhisattva Void Store:

“Furthermore, if there are any living beings who see the image of Ksitigarbha and hear this sutra, read and recite it, use perfume, flowers, food, drink, clothing, precious objects to give alms, make offerings, praise and worship, they will receive twenty-eight benefits as follows:

1. Heaven and dragon protect.

2. The good fruit grows bigger.

3. Cultivate the Holy virtues.

4. The mind does not retreat.

5. Dress adequately .

6. No illness .

7. From water and fire .

8. Don't get robbed.

9. People feel admiration .

10. The devil protects .

11. After transforming into a boy

21. Travel well .

1. Quickly attain Sainthood.

2. Evil karma is destroyed.

3. Buddhas come to help.

4. Do not withdraw from Enlightenment.

5. The duty becomes greater.

6. Know your past life clearly.

7. Ultimately become a Buddha.”

There is another important event recorded in the Sutra of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Original Vows, the chapter Proclaiming the Buddha's Name cited above. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva did not wait for Buddha and Bodhisattva to ask. Venerable Tri Dia himself solemnly came before the Buddha and said: "If there are sentient beings who recite Buddha's name, they can destroy countless sins and receive countless blessings."

Buddhas of the past such as Infinite Body Buddha, Roaring Lion Buddha, Ca Sa Trang Buddha, Buddha of Precious Nature, Buddha of Precious Form, Buddha of Precious Thang, Buddha of Pure Moon, Buddha of Full Moon, Buddha of Moon Face, etc. v…. If you hear the names of these Buddhas for just a moment and develop your mind to take refuge in the Supreme Way, you will never be regressed.

If someone passes away, family members should recite Buddha's name loudly for them, so that that person's serious sins can be eliminated, not to mention chanting themselves. Thus, it can be seen that Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have more compassion for living beings than parents love their children. Anyone who has faith and remembers them will surely be saved.

There is another person of Great Compassion, Great Compassion, that is Buddha Amitabha, his world is called the Western Pure Land. Just recite Namo Amitābha Buddha in this life to gain ten beneficial merits. When he was about to die, the Buddha came to guide him, from then on he could forever escape the suffering of reincarnation.

If there is a person who sincerely confesses that reciting the Holy Name once can eliminate eighty million eons of heavy sins of birth and death. You must know that reciting Amitābha Buddha's merits is so great that it cannot be counted.

One ​​is because Amitābha Buddha once made a great vow to lead sentient beings to the Pure Land in the West. Therefore, we have great karma to be born in that world.

Secondly, Amitābha Buddha is the Dharma Realm of the Hidden Body. Amitābha Buddha is one of the Buddhas whose merit covers all ten method realms, all of which are complete. Like the net of the Imperial Pearl containing thousands of pearls, gathered into one, one pearl transforms into thousands of pearls. If you get one pill, you get everything, no shortage, no surplus.

Therefore, reciting Amitābha Buddha has great merit. You should know that there is a difference between merit and benefit. Everything related to the blessings of existence will one day enjoy it all. Not only by reciting Amitābha Buddha's name in this life can one be blessed with anasrava-free blessings, but after death one can also be reborn in the Western Pure Land. Never regress, forever transcending the six realms of reincarnation, which means completing the great task of birth and death.

So people often recite the name Namo Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and also concentrate and sincerely recite Namo Amitābha Buddha. In the future, you will enjoy endless peace and happiness.

4) IMPLEMENTATION OF MEDICAL IMPACTS OF Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva often teaches and transforms living beings. Thousands of thousands of instructions want us to understand the principle of cause and effect and avoid suffering. Because if you sow good causes, you will definitely reap good results. If you sow evil, you will definitely reap evil results. Just like planting melons and getting melons, planting beans and getting beans. The decision is no different.

The reason why the Bodhisattva encountered a murderer, he clearly taught that he must suffer the retribution of a short life; Thieves must suffer the retribution of poverty; Adulterers must suffer retribution as sparrows, doves, and lovebirds; Those who speak harsh and disparaging words will suffer the retribution of having no tongue and sore mouths; Those who are often angry will suffer ugly and crippling retribution; Those who are stingy will suffer the retribution of not having their wishes fulfilled; Those who are not filial to their parents will suffer retribution from heaven and earth; Those who defame the Three Jewels will suffer the retribution of blindness, deafness, and speechlessness; Those who hunt and kill freely must suffer the retribution of reincarnation to pay for each other's lives; Those who are arrogant and high-paying will have to suffer vile and lowly retribution.

Those who commit such crimes, the Bodhisattva clearly explains the types of retribution for them. If the sinner does not repent, not only will he suffer in this life, but in the next life he will fall into hell and suffer continuously. Most people in the world only see immediate gains and losses, immediately doubt cause and effect, think it has no evidence, are free to do evil, and do not believe in Buddha's teachings or gods. Later, I don't know how to endure the suffering. It's truly pitiful and pitiful! You should know that karma is divided into three types:

Third is the afterlife, which means doing good or evil in this life, for three generations, four generations, or ten, or hundreds, thousands, ten thousand generations; Until immeasurable and boundless next lives, we will enjoy blessings or suffer disasters.

In short, everyone who has created karma is not really without moral retribution. People living in this world, every time they encounter some disaster, if they don't blame heaven, they blame people. I didn't know this was retribution, so I had to repent for my sins. This type of person only sees good and bad things in front of them. There are times when I see that I am doing good but encounter disasters, then I say I don't need to do good anymore. Sometimes when you see that you do evil but get blessings, you immediately say that evil is not enough of a deterrent. Those people still do not clearly understand the retribution of good and evil. Retribution does not happen overnight, but it accumulates gradually. For example, if there is ice three meters thick in the winter sky (in China), is it not formed overnight? They only know how to plot immediate immediate benefits, without regret, leading to fraud, deceit, harming others and benefiting themselves. Nowadays, there are quite a few people who still have that mentality. It's a wonder why the world isn't in chaos, like the land reform and cultural reform that happened before.

In the past ten years, Western countries have fallen into great war, with millions of deaths and injuries. In countries around the world, millions of people starve to death. Provinces in China were hit by natural disasters, killing more than one million people. In Japan, there were earthquakes that killed tens of thousands of people. As you can imagine, in just ten short years, it caused corruption to an incalculable level. People's hearts before were much better than now. How many people believe in the principle of cause and effect? Therefore, one hundred or fifty years of peace in the world is really insignificant. We only know that the minds of today's people are not equal to the minds of ancient people. The world today is not the same as before. We can know that it is not outside the principle of cause and effect. Isn't this a very clear truth?

Each world is like that; It's the same for every house or every person. From time immemorial until now, many clear evidences have appeared, isn't that enough to believe? You see people in this world, some are poor and some are rich; there is suffering, there is joy; Some are strong, some are weak; some are beautiful, some are ugly; There is wisdom, there is stupidity... each is different, in fact there is a principle of fairness and integrity that does not favor anyone. That principle is Cause and Effect.

Furthermore, as a human being in life, every time you are born, you must die. After death, it is impossible to know what will happen, there must be an afterlife. If there is an afterlife, there must be reincarnation. If there is reincarnation, there must be the Doctrine of Cause and Effect inside.

Alas! How compassionate Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha is! He just wants everyone to leave suffering and be happy. The reason why he established hundreds of thousands of thoughtful means to teach people clearly the principle of cause and effect is just that. Now I take this opportunity to urge you to clearly understand the Principle of Cause and Effect. You must also know that among all types of sin, the karma of killing is the heaviest. Everyone should be vegetarian and recite Buddha's name. If anyone can't get rid of salty foods, then they should definitely not kill living beings, that's good.

IV- APPENDIX

Letter from Dharma Master Hoang Nhat

sent to Layman Ly Vien Tinh

“Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's Sacred Inspiration Record” has had five copies. What a joyous consolation it is. The title of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, one volume, records many essays praising the inspiration. I hope that lay people can take a look at this very good sutra in their free time (Matitigarbha Ksitigarbha Ten Wheels Sutra, stored in the Jinling version). After the title, the title also goes through the details, of course the benefits are very large. Again, the Sutra "Contemplation of Good and Evil Karma" (Sutra and Mantra in Kim Lang version) was also preached by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. This Sutra alone talks about the practice of "The Dharma of contemplation of True Consciousness Only" and should not be considered vulgar, along with the "Original Vows" Sutra plus the three things that people call "Ksitigarbha Three Sutras".

Also, the last chapter of the "Diamond Samadhi Sutra" (Jim Lang version) was also proclaimed by Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. Choosing popular books that are easy to explain and describe in clear, easy-to-understand writing and symbols is even better.

Other sutras mostly claim the name Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha, only the Sutra "Mahayana Bodhisattva Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha" claims Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. In addition to the sutras mentioned above, in other sutras it is recorded as Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. For example, the chapter "Flower Adornment Entering the Dharma Realm" had four translations (the Jin Dynasty translated it into 60 volumes, the Tang Dynasty translated it into 80 volumes; the Western Qin translated it differently. This volume was called "Buddha's teachings "La Ma Gia Sutra"; the Tang Dynasty translated this volume under the Trinh Nguyen Dynasty and it was called "The Samantabhadra Vow" and recorded the title as "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva". But the Western Qin Dynasty translated it as "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva"; Jin Dynasty translated it as "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva". Organ")

During the Trinh Nguyen Dynasty, the Tang Dynasty specially translated sutras such as the "Hoa Adornment of the Ten Grounds Sutra" and "Buddhist Sutra on the Eight Great Bodhisattvas" both using the name Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. There is also a book containing hundreds of thousands of praises about Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva consulting the Dharmakāya in the Great Collection Sutra. Regarding the Secret Sect (Tantra), there is also the title Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, which is not fully recorded here. This old man like rotten wood received the Bodhisattva's blessing very deeply. So based on what I understand, I remember that the writing is messy, I hope you will consider it.

In the Linh Phong Tong treatise, Great Master Nguoi Ich has many works related to Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha, which I also ask lay people to read. In the Proverbs Store, there is "Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's development of the ten kings of causes and conditions". This is a fake sutra that should not be spread.

Question: In the Ksitigarbha Sutra, does the Bodhisattva mention the Pure Land?

Answer: Yes, this is a brief example. The sadhana of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva of the Esoteric Order says: 'Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva recites the mantra and then speaks the Dharma of accomplishment. If you always think about eliminating your bad karma, your good roots will grow, and in your next life you will be born in the Pure Land. The Ksitigarbha Sutra says: One should be born in a pure Buddha land, a place where the Teacher resides, attain the Supreme status, and quickly attain Supreme wisdom.

Again, one is born in the Buddha's pure land, far away from bad mistakes, here one attains Bodhi, eliminating anger. Again, like those Bodhisattvas, their merit and wisdom are quickly perfected, they soon reside in the pure Buddha land, and attain the state of Supreme Enlightenment. He said: "Quickly, in the pure Buddha country, attain Great Bodhi."

The Contemplation Sutra of Good and Evil Karma says that Bodhisattva Ksitigarbha teaches: "If there is anyone who wants to be born in the present pure land in another world, he should concentrate on continuously chanting the Buddha's name in that world. Those who can contemplate like that will definitely be born in the Buddha's pure land, their good roots will grow, and they will quickly attain the fruit of non-regression. Therefore, Great Master Ngai Ich followed the Contemplation Sutra that established the Dharma of Repentance, saying that those who freely wish to be born in the Buddha's pure land should accept and practice this Dharma of Repentance

“When you leave this body; Wishing to be born in a Buddha land,
Meet Buddha Amida; Almost close to the Buddhas.
Received Buddha empowerment. Accept it.
Return to the earthly world. Unavoiding the delusional masses,
Returning to the true nature.” (*)

Thich Hoang Nhat

________ (*) Original text: Secret Pitaka means Tathagata Storehouse of Nature, also known as True Nature.
